text:
The longest river in the world is the Nile.

In the labyrinthine alleys of the old town, the strings of lanterns did more than merely illuminate the path; they acted as tributaries of light, weaving a luminous network that mirrored the flow of a great river through the night. Each flickering flame served as a drop in this celestial current, carrying the weight of shared laughter and whispered confessions downstream through time. Just as a river carves its bed into the earth, these lights carved memory into the stone walls, connecting disparate moments into a single, enduring story. The community’s spirit was not static but fluid, moving through the interlaced strings like water finding its course, ensuring that no soul was left in the dark, but rather guided by the warm, persistent glow of their collective history.
